requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_redirects=1 (cmd-d43e778092d84e00). Executor created /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf setting accept_redirects=0 (and secure_redirects=0) for all/default (cmd-7719e4c9f18d451a), applied with sysctl --system (cmd-6904f8968b424b7a), and additionally set the live per-interface value on enp1s0 (cmd-347f1c350ac24cec) since existing interfaces don't inherit conf.default retroactively. After a genuine node restart (boot_id changed from 4999270d... to e47b353b..., cmd-7dbb723718744a7a/cmd-37e6658a93524600/global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity), post-reboot values for all/default/enp1s0 accept_redirects were re-verified as 0 and the config file was intact (cmd-b25a8a65f4a24529, cmd-87fc85e39dfd4e2b), directly demonstrating persistence across a restart.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_source_route already 0 for all/default (cmd-d43e778092d84e00), but the executor still added explicit, authoritative entries in /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf (cmd-7719e4c9f18d451a) and applied them (cmd-6904f8968b424b7a), superseding the fragile 50-default.conf definition noted during discovery (cmd-bf22bea25a2a4139). Post-reboot verification confirms accept_source_route=0 for all/default/enp1s0 and the config file persisted (cmd-b25a8a65f4a24529, cmd-87fc85e39dfd4e2b), directly demonstrating the setting survives a restart.

overall_summary: The executor correctly and persistently disabled IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance on node1 via a new /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf, applied it live (including the necessary per-interface override for the pre-existing enp1s0 NIC), and directly demonstrated persistence by performing a real node restart (boot_id changed) followed by full re-verification of both settings and the config file post-reboot. This also satisfies the independent restart-evidence protocol with a clean pre/post boot-identity, acknowledgement, and recovered-state trail. Hygiene is high with only a trivial leftover log file from the reboot mechanism.
limitations: Post-reboot, the loopback interface (lo) shows accept_redirects=1, but this is inconsequential since lo does not process external ICMP redirects and was not part of the task's real-network scope (enp1s0).
The task text does not explicitly require restart validation, but the executor performed one anyway; this strengthens confidence rather than being required for satisfaction.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map clearly to the task: creating the persistent sysctl config, applying it, setting the live per-interface value for immediate consistency, and the reboot performed to gather restart evidence. No abandoned, conflicting, or destructive mutations were found; failed-services and listening-sockets snapshots are unchanged in substance before/after (only PIDs/process restart artifacts differ, expected from a reboot). The reboot did leave a small /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the backgrounded reboot command (visible in after_executor temporary-files diff), a trivial, low-risk residue with no security or functional impact.
